title_en: Taifu Food Co., Ltd. v. Taishan Enterprise Co., Ltd. — appeal of unfair competition dispute
keywords_en: Civil; Unfair competition dispute; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Fujian Province; Taiwan Province; Legal person; Anti-Unfair Competition Law; Patent Law; Exclusive right to packaging and decoration; Determination of prior use; Time of market entry; Affirm the original judgment; Similarity of packaging and decoration; Sale of Taiwan products in Mainland China; Invalidity of design patent; Patent right; Unfair competition; Patent invalidity; Unfair competition dispute of a limited company
full_text_en:
Taifu Food Co., Ltd. v. Taishan Enterprise Co., Ltd. — dispute over unfair competition (appeal)

Appellant (defendant at first instance, counterclaim plaintiff): Taifu Food Co., Ltd. Domicile: Dongwu Industrial Zone, Wenling Town, Changle City, Fujian Province.

Legal representative: Chen Meijin, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Fucong, lawyer of Beijing Horizon Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Chen Jiali, Deputy General Manager of the Company.

Appellee (plaintiff at first instance, counterclaim defendant): Taishan Enterprise Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 501, Section 2, Fuzhen Road, Renmei Li, Yuanlin Town, Changhua County, Taiwan Province.

Legal representative: Zhan Rendoa, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Liguang, patent agent of Beijing Aorui Patent Agency.

Agent ad litem: Li Jianmin, Manager of the Legal Affairs Section of the Company.

The appellant Taifu Food Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Taifu Company), dissatisfied with the civil judgment of first instance rendered by the Fujian High People's Court in the case of dispute over unfair competition with the appellee Taishan Enterprise Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Taishan Company), filed an appeal to the Supreme People's Court.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial:

The plaintiff Taishan Company was registered and established in Changhua County, Taiwan Province, in 1950. In 1986, Taishan Company registered in Taiwan the packaging pattern composed of "grass-green grass jelly cube blocks" for its "Herbal Jelly" drink and the mark "Taishan" as a trademark, and began production of "Eight Treasure Congee" in the same year. After 1993, the above two products were sold to the mainland region of China.

On October 17, 1994, Taifu Company filed two applications for design patents with the Patent Office of China. Among them, the design patent for "Eight Treasure Congee (can sheet material)" was granted on November 26, 1995, with patent number ZL9431207X; the design patent for "Beverage Can Sheet Material (Herbal Jelly)" was granted on January 7, 1996, with patent number ZL94312074.8. The plaintiff Taishan Company, believing that the packaging patterns, colors, and text of the two beverages produced by Taifu Company were similar to its own products, filed a request with the Patent Office of China to declare the above two design patents of Taifu Company invalid, and brought an action on the grounds that the acts of Taifu Company constituted unfair competition, requesting a judgment ordering Taifu Company to immediately cease infringement, compensate for economic losses, and bear the litigation costs of this case. The defendant Taifu Company filed a counterclaim on the grounds that Taishan Company had infringed its design patent rights, requesting a judgment ordering Taishan Company to immediately cease infringement and compensate for corresponding economic losses. On March 28, 1997, the Patent Reexamination Board of the Patent Office of China made a final decision declaring the above two patent rights of Taifu Company invalid.

The court of first instance held that: The patent rights of the defendant Taifu Company have been declared invalid. Pursuant to Article 50, paragraph 1 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, the patent rights are deemed to have never existed from the beginning. The plaintiff Taishan Company had produced and sold "Herbal Jelly" and "Eight Treasure Congee" beverages in Taiwan before the patent application date of Taifu Company, and began selling them in the mainland region in the early 1990s. Taifu Company used packaging patterns, colors, and text structures similar to those of Taishan Company on the same products, which was sufficient to mislead consumers and cause confusion between the two. According to Article 5, Item (2) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, this constitutes an act of unfair competition, infringing upon the legitimate rights and interests of Taishan Company and causing certain damage to Taishan Company. Pursuant to Article 20 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, Taifu Company shall bear liability for compensation. The counterclaim of Taifu Company against Taishan Company for infringement of its design patent rights, requesting a judgment ordering Taishan Company to cease infringement and compensate for losses, lacks evidence and is not supported. Accordingly, the court of first instance ruled: 1. Taifu Company shall immediately cease producing products whose packaging can appearance patterns are similar to those of the "Taishan" brand Herbal Jelly and Eight Treasure Congee beverages of Taishan Company; 2. Taifu Company shall compensate Taishan Company for economic losses of RMB 21,000 and attorney's fees of RMB 20,000. The case acceptance fee of RMB 21,000, the litigation preservation fee of RMB 5,000, and the counterclaim fee of RMB 5,510 shall all be borne by Taifu Company.

Taifu Company appealed, arguing: 1. Although the "Herbal Jelly" and "Eight Treasure Congee" beverages produced by the appellee Taishan Company were sold in the state-owned foreign currency duty-free shops of the Xiamen Special Economic Zone from the end of 1993 to the end of 1994, because the customers of such shops were specific and the goods sold were subject to strict supervision and restrictions, it cannot be considered that they had entered the market within the territory of China. 2. The earliest date when the "Herbal Jelly" and "Eight Treasure Congee" beverages of Taishan Company were legally sold to the mainland was April 6, 1995. The finding in the judgment of first instance that Taishan Company had sold the aforementioned two products to the mainland in the early 1990s lacks factual basis. 3. The appellant had already started marketing "Herbal Jelly" and "Eight Treasure Congee" beverages as early as August 1994. Since the appellant's products were sold first, while Taishan Company sold "Herbal Jelly" and "Eight Treasure Congee" beverages with packaging and decoration similar to those of the appellant's products in the mainland market later, the real unfair competitor is Taishan Company, not the appellant. Therefore, Taifu Company requested the reversal of the judgment of first instance.

The appellee Taishan Company argued in defense: The judgment of first instance found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and should be affirmed.

Upon trial, the Supreme People's Court, in addition to confirming that the facts found by the first instance were substantially true, also found: The packaging and decoration used by the appellee Taishan Company for its "Herbal Jelly" beverage mainly consisted of the three Chinese characters "仙草蜜" in running script and a "grass-green grass jelly cube block" pattern. The packaging and decoration used for the "Eight Treasure Congee" beverage mainly consisted of the three Chinese characters "八宝粥" in running script and a "colorful pattern of eight treasure congee placed in a bowl". The above two beverages enjoyed a relatively high reputation in Taiwan and other regions. From the end of 1993 to the end of 1994, Taishan Company imported "Herbal Jelly" and "Eight Treasure Congee" beverages bearing the above packaging and decoration into the mainland through Hong Kong, and sold them in the state-owned foreign currency duty-free shop of the Xiamen Special Economic Zone, and later sold them in the state-owned foreign currency duty-free shop of the Shantou Special Economic Zone. This fact is proven by evidence including the "Statement" issued by the state-owned foreign currency duty-free shop of the Xiamen Special Economic Zone, the "Statement" issued by Feng Liqin Trading Co., Ltd. (Hong Kong), the "Health Certificate" issued by the Xiamen Import Food Hygiene Supervision and Inspection Institute of the People's Republic of China, the "Health Certificate" issued by the Shantou Import Food Hygiene Supervision and Inspection Institute of the People's Republic of China, as well as relevant contracts, bills of lading, and invoices. In August 1994, the appellant Taifu Company also began producing and selling "Herbal Jelly" and "Eight Treasure Congee" beverages. The packaging and decoration used for the two products were substantially identical to those of Taishan Company. Among them, the manufacturer's name and address printed in English on the packaging can of the "Herbal Jelly" beverage produced by Taifu Company were the name and address of Taishan Company.

The Supreme People's Court held that: The appellee Taishan Company had continuously produced and sold "Taishan" brand "Herbal Jelly" and "Eight Treasure Congee" beverages since 1986, using the aforementioned packaging and decoration. These two products enjoyed a relatively high reputation in the Taiwan region. Starting from the end of 1993, Taishan Company began selling the "Herbal Jelly" and "Eight Treasure Congee" beverages bearing the aforementioned packaging and decoration in the state-owned foreign currency duty-free shop of the Xiamen Special Economic Zone, earlier than the appellant Taifu Company's first use of the packaging and decoration for the above two products in the mainland market, and enjoyed a certain reputation among the relevant public. Therefore, Taishan Company has the exclusive right to use the distinctive packaging and decoration of the "Herbal Jelly" and "Eight Treasure Congee" products in the mainland region, which shall be protected by law. Without permission from Taishan Company, Taifu Company, on the same goods it produced, used packaging and decoration substantially identical to those of Taishan Company, which was sufficient to cause consumer confusion. Its act has constituted unfair competition and shall bear corresponding civil legal liability. The state-owned foreign currency duty-free shops in the special economic zones are also part of the domestic market of China. The state's supervision and restriction of goods sold in such shops are administrative measures to regulate the variety and quantity of foreign goods entering the domestic market of China. The adoption of such administrative measures by the state does not prove that the industrial property rights enjoyed by the manufacturer of the regulated goods for such goods are not protected by the laws of China. Therefore, Taifu Company's ground of appeal that goods sold in the state-owned foreign currency duty-free shops of the special economic zones cannot be considered as having entered the domestic market of China cannot be established. Taifu Company's ground of appeal that the "Herbal Jelly" and "Eight Treasure Congee" beverages of Taishan Company were only legally sold to the mainland market as late as April 1995, and its ground of appeal that it first used the aforementioned packaging and decoration for the "Herbal Jelly" and "Eight Treasure Congee" beverages in the mainland, are also inconsistent with the facts and are not accepted. The judgment of first instance found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and should be affirmed. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Supreme People's Court ruled on July 27, 1998:

Appeal dismissed, and the original judgment affirmed.

The case acceptance fee for the second instance of RMB 21,000 shall be borne by Taifu Company.
